features: MONEY LANDING ON THE WRONG PERSON, WITH THE BOOKS BALANCING — No migration: the database is not touched. This closes the chain of four proportions, the common root of the calculation defects fixed over the past two months.

WHY THESE DEFECTS ARE INVISIBLE. To turn a cost into shares the engine runs four proportions in a row, then renormalises. That means whatever goes missing along the way, the plan total always matches the budget: everything balances, no accounting check has anything to report. The defect does not show up as «the books don't balance» but as money charged to the wrong person with perfect books. That is why they surface one at a time, and only someone who really manages a building can spot them.

THIRD LINK — THE SPLIT BY ROLE. An expense item states how much of a unit's share falls to the owner, how much to the tenant, how much to the usufructuary. If those percentages added up to less than 100, the unattributed part did not vanish: it was absorbed and charged anyway. Measured: two units, a cost of € 1,000.00, a split declaring 60% → € 1,000.00 charged. That undeclared part is now treated as uncovered, it halts plan generation, and you can only proceed by stating a reason — exactly as already happened for table coefficients.

AND THE DOOR THAT LET IT THROUGH. Four places in the program write those percentages. Three checked that they added up to 100; the item edit card did not. It does now, and from this version an automated check verifies that no new place can write without checking.

FOURTH LINK — A HOLDER WITH A ZERO SHARE. If a unit's tenant is on record but with a zero share, they do not pay: so far so good. The problem was where their part ended up. Measured: two units, a cost of € 1,000.00 split half owner and half tenant, and on the second unit a tenant with a zero share → the first unit paid € 666.67 and the second € 333.33. That is € 166.67 moved from one unit to another, with the plan total exact to the cent.

HOW THE RIGHT BEHAVIOUR WAS DECIDED: by comparing it with the same case with no tenant at all. There the program already did the sensible thing — the share stays with the owner of that same unit — because a dedicated rule resolves the missing role. The two situations are the same thing: nobody paying that half on that unit. From now on a role whose shares are all zero is treated as an absent role, and takes the same path.

WHAT HAS NOT CHANGED, AND IT IS A STATED CHOICE: if a unit has a single recorded holder with a 50% share, they still pay the unit's whole share. The cost must be paid by someone, and if only one holder is on record it falls to them. Co-owners likewise keep splitting the share between themselves. Both cases are now pinned by an automated check, so the choice stays visible rather than indistinguishable from an oversight.

UNDER THE BONNET: eleven new checks, four of which pin the healthy cases so the fix cannot shift them by a cent. Both fixes live in the engine and not only in the screens: a new door tomorrow would reopen the same hole, and data written before today remains.
